coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Channel Lane

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt) on the undivided remainder lot 8719A006; edges are Blocks J's and I's traced edges (~1-3 m) and the TAFB property line / unbuilt Bridgeview Street line.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figure 6.2 (p.151), Figure 3.1.1 - Location Map of Open Spaces (p.45) and Section 3.4 Channel Lane (p.66).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this open space -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this open space touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated open space, Design Controls Section 3.4: a 50 ft maximum plaza with a 12 ft pedestrian throughway, not accessible by vehicles, a view corridor that Guideline 3.4.4 says should be maintained from Mission Rock Square to the water (a guideline, not a standard), connecting across Terry A Francois Boulevard to Channel Wharf.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock Design Controls, which name this planned open space as Channel Lane (Design Controls Section 3.4); the Port's Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested this approval under Resolution 18-04, and its Sept 2019 memo dates the Commission's approvals January 30, 2018 (it numbers the Design Controls resolution 18-05)

sources.title: Port Commission Item 11A staff report, Jan 26 2018 (request); Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sept 20 2019 (approval date)

milestones.source: Port Commission Item 11A staff report, Jan 26 2018 (request); Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sept 20 2019 (approval date)

changes.text: The geometry notes said Channel Lane has a protected view corridor and that it is not yet built with surface parking there today. The Design Controls call the view corridor a guideline ('should be maintained'), not a protected standard, and a 2018 plan cannot show today's condition. The notes now say that and cite the Port's June 2026 report; the lane's built state is not confirmed. The Jan 30, 2018 Design Controls approval milestone and changelog row now cite the Sept 2019 Port memo that states the date.
Channel Lane added: the planned pedestrian open space between Blocks J and I, from the Design Controls' open space plan.
changes.source: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figures 1.1 and 3.1.1, Section 3.4; Port Commission Item 7A memo, Sept 20 2019 (January 30, 2018 approval)

record.notes: Planned pedestrian lane between Blocks J and I (Design Controls Section 3.4, Figure 1.1). No source read shows it built: the Port's June 5, 2026 report describes the project site as a surface parking lot to be transformed and Phase 2, not yet begun, as possibly starting construction as early as 2027. Its own current condition is not separately confirmed.
